findings.title: All-clients permission is ignored once a client has any per-client permission
findings.description:
`hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` only falls back to the all-clients `Clients` resource when no resource named after the client exists. If one does exist, it evaluates only that resource.

- **Why the fallback is lost:** per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (lines 103-111) without `setType(...)`. `DefaultPolicyEvaluator` (lines 70-82) only adds type-level policies when `resource.getType() != null`.
- **Effect:** an admin granted `manage` on all clients loses `canManage`, `canConfigure`, `canMapRoles` etc. on client X as soon as anyone creates any permission on X, even one for a different admin or scope.
- **Inconsistency:** `canView(ClientModel)` checks the all-clients `canView()` first, so `view` behaves differently from the other scopes.
- **Docs disagree:** the new Javadoc on `ClientPermissionEvaluator.canManage(ClientModel)` and its siblings promises the "all clients" grant applies.

`UserPermissionsV2` has the same pattern, but this is new code and no test covers the combination.

findings.title: `getClientsWithPermission` in V2 can never return client IDs
findings.description:
`resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` runs the `findResourceIdByType` query, which filters on `r.type = :type`. Only the schema-level `Clients` resource has that type; per-client resources have none.

The method therefore returns either an empty set or the literal `"Clients"`, never a client ID. The one caller, `AvailableRoleMappingResource.java:229-230`, does `realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream()` and would hit a null pointer on `"Clients"`. That caller is currently gated on the V1 feature flag, so the override is effectively dead and untested.

findings.title: Token exchange now fails with HTTP 500 under V2 instead of a clean denial
findings.description:
`canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. It is called unconditionally from `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToClient` (line 276) via `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients()`.

That path is reachable from `V1TokenExchangeProvider` (line 154), whose `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` feature has no dependency on FGAP V1. With `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` on, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`. Before this diff the same call reached the V1 implementation and returned `false`, giving a 403 `access_denied`. The inherited two-argument overload delegates to the same method. Returning `false` would keep the deny semantics.

findings.title: Null pointer when the type-level resource cannot be resolved
findings.description:
`AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource` returns `null` when `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false or the `Clients` resource is missing. The result goes straight into `findByResource(server, resource)`, which dereferences `resource.getId()` (`JPAPolicyStore.java:215`).

This state is reachable: `RealmManager.java:567-570` imports an `adminPermissionsClient` and creates its resource server without requiring `adminPermissionsEnabled`. Every `canManage`/`canView(client)` check for an admin without the global role would then throw instead of denying. `hasPermission(String)` at lines 244-247 guards the null correctly; the two helpers should match.

findings.title: Client removal has no V2 cleanup
findings.description: The listener is now gated on the V1 feature. That gate is necessary, because `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws. But under V2 nothing removes the per-client resource or its scope permissions from the admin-permissions resource server when a client is deleted. Orphaned resources and permissions accumulate with no test or TODO marking the gap.

findings.title: Dead code and triplicated evaluation logic in `ClientPermissionsV2`
findings.description:
- **Unused members:** the private `getEvaluationContext(...)` is never called, and the `logger` field (line 51) is unused.
- **Unused imports:** `Scope`, `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, and `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext` (needed only by the dead method).
- **Duplication:** the "evaluate and look for scope" loop appears three times (lines 224-234, 249-259, 274-286) and a fourth time in the parent's private `ClientPermissions.hasPermission(Resource, String)`.
- **Needless wrapping:** `Arrays.asList(scope)` plus `contains` for a single string.
- **Visibility:** the class is `public` with a public constructor taking the package-private `MgmtPermissionsV2`, and extends the package-private `ClientPermissions`. The sibling `UserPermissionsV2` is package-private.

findings.title: Javadoc describes `void` require-methods as returning `true`
findings.description: `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` are documented as "Returns `true` if …". Both are `void` and throw `ForbiddenException`; the other `require*` docs in the same diff get this right. The "For V2 only: also … all clients" statements on the per-client methods are also inaccurate, per the first finding. The file uses `<p/>` throughout, which Javadoc doclint rejects as a self-closing element.

findings.title: New tests miss several new code paths, and one assertion does not test what it claims
findings.description:
- **Vacuous assertion:** in `testManageOnlyOneClient` the `ForbiddenException` comes from `getDefaultClientScopes()`, so `removeDefaultClientScope` is never exercised without the permission.
- **Untested paths:**
  - `canMapClientScopeRoles` (`map-roles-client-scope`)
  - `getClientsWithPermission`
  - `canManageClientScopes`, `canManage(ClientScopeModel)` and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` via the client-scopes endpoints
  - negative per-client permissions
  - an all-clients grant combined with a per-client permission
  - client deletion while permissions exist

The defects in the first, second and fifth findings sit exactly in these gaps.

findings.title: Tests mutate shared realm state without cleanup
findings.description:
`@AfterEach` removes only permissions; the policies are removed via `realm.cleanup()`. Everything else persists on the shared `myclient`/`myadmin` fixtures from `RealmAdminPermissionsConfig`:

- **`testConfigureOnlyOneClient`:** regenerates the secret of `myclient`, the client `realmAdminClient` authenticates with (configured as `mysecret`). Any later token re-acquisition in the class would use a stale secret.
- **`testManageOnlyOneClient`:** renames `myclient` and moves a default client scope to optional (lines 166-178).
- **`testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient`:** creates two client roles and a role mapping on `myadmin` (lines 331-364).

This makes the methods order-dependent and non-repeatable.

findings.title: JUnit 4 `Assert.fail` used in a JUnit 5 test
findings.description: The file imports `org.junit.Assert.fail` alongside `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions`; it is the only file in the `fgap` test package that does. Use `Assertions.fail` or, better, `assertThrows(ForbiddenException.class, ...)` in place of the repeated try/fail/catch blocks.

findings.title: Inconsistent helper style in `AbstractPermissionTest`
findings.description:
- **Shadowing:** helpers were made `static` with a `ManagedClient client` parameter that shadows the inherited `client` field every caller passes.
- **Mixed style:** `getPolicies()` (line 58) and the two `createPermission(ManagedClient, ...)` overloads at lines 163-179 remain instance methods.
- **Unused helper:** `createClientPolicy` (line 136) is never called.
- **Roundabout call:** `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest` builds `UserConfigBuilder.create().id(newUserId).build().getId()` just to get `newUserId` back.

findings.title: `Clients` type only partly wired into `AdminPermissionsSchema`
findings.description:
- **Display names:** `getResourceName` still special-cases only `USERS`. Client resources fall through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, so `PolicyResourceService.java:218` gets no "All clients" label and no clientId.
- **Shared namespace:** user and client resources share one name space keyed by raw ID, and `getOrCreateResource` looks up by name regardless of type. The overlapping `manage`/`view`/`map-roles` scopes are separated only by ID uniqueness.
- **Whitespace:** line 53 introduces trailing whitespace.

findings.title: Schema registration and V2 wiring
findings.description:
- **Schema:** the `CLIENTS` resource type, its scopes and `resolveClient` (ID then clientId fallback) mirror the existing `USERS` handling correctly.
- **Wiring:** `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` lazily caches the V2 instance like `users()`.
- **Fail-closed checks:** role checks precede policy evaluation, `isAdminSameRealm()` and a null resource server deny, and `findByName(server, id, server.getId())` matches the default owner because `ResourceServerAdapter.getClientId()` returns `getId()`.
- **Management endpoints:** the V1-only endpoints in `ClientResource` (lines 706, 739) are feature-gated, so the `UnsupportedOperationException` overrides for them are unreachable under V2.
